QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_26

question.text: A domestic client has a gross open position of USD 22 million in USDINR futures and options. The total market-wide open interest in USDINR is USD 300 million. Under SEBI/RBI rules, the client-level gross open position limit is the higher of 6% of total open interest or USD 20 million. What action will the exchange take?

answer.text: The client has breached the applicable limit (higher of 6% of USD 300 million = USD 18 million, or USD 20 million, i.e. USD 20 million); the exchange will restrain the client from taking further positions, facilitate close-out of the excess and may levy a penalty
The exchange will automatically square off the entire USD 22 million position at market price
The client can continue trading as the USD 20 million figure is only a floor and never binds
No action is needed because the client-level limit for domestic clients in USDINR is a fixed USD 50 million

explanation.text: The Logic: For USDINR futures and options, the domestic client-level gross open position limit is the HIGHER of 6% of total open interest or USD 20 million. Here, 6% of USD 300 million = USD 18 million, which is lower than the USD 20 million floor, so the applicable limit is USD 20 million. The client's USD 22 million position exceeds this. The exchange restrains further position build-up, facilitates close-out of the excess and may levy a penalty. The Trap: USD 20 million is not a fixed client limit — it is a floor under the higher-of rule. When 6% of total OI is higher than USD 20 million, the higher figure becomes the limit. The exchange does not auto-square off the entire position; it restricts further positions, facilitates close-out and may impose penalties. Note: The higher-of rule means client limits grow with market open interest, but never fall below the USD 20 million floor. Always check both the percentage-of-OI figure and the absolute floor before sizing a position.
